{{< include ../../_include/_title_meta_items.qmd >}}

Verification consumes up to 70 percent of chip project effort. A single
bug at advanced nodes costs tens of millions to respin. Every existing
approach -- random simulation, formal property checking, manual
inspection -- leaves the same gap: the full cross product of instruction
fields is never exhaustively visited because the combinatorial space is
too large for standard Cartesian enumeration.

Project-E redefines verification as structural enumeration rather than
statistical sampling. Verification becomes a complete map of what the
design can and cannot do, and that map accumulates across runs as a
persistent corporate asset. When multiple specifications are coordinated,
each reveals constraints that no single pass can detect. Parallel
verification scales linearly with available cores -- no coordination,
no merging, no cross-talk.

Current validation is open across multiple processor architectures.
